1.title: Andhra History: Firsts and State Formation

mcqs.question: The first linguistic state of Andhra was formed in which month and year?
mcqs.explanation: The first linguistic state of Andhra was formed in April 1953 after separation from Madras.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: Tanguturi Prakasam was the first Chief Minister of Andhra State in 1953.
Chandulal Madhavlal Trivedi was the first Governor of Andhra Pradesh.
Bezawada Gopala Reddy was the last Chief Minister of Andhra State.
Neelam Sanjiva Reddy was the first Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh in 1956.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect statement is the third one. Chandulal Madhavlal Trivedi was the first Governor of Andhra Pradesh, while the first Governor of Andhra Pradesh was Chandulal Madhavlal Trivedi; the altered detail is the office description in relation to the other listed state offices.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Andhra became the first linguistic state in 1953.
Reason (R): Andhra State was formed in April 1953 after separation from Madras.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The formation of Andhra State in April 1953 after separation from Madras established it as the first linguistic state.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(a) First Chief Minister of Andhra State
(b) First Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh
(c) First Governor of Andhra Pradesh
(d) First Speaker of Andhra State

List-II
(i) Chandulal Madhavlal Trivedi
(ii) Tanguturi Prakasam
(iii) Neelam Sanjiva Reddy
(iv) Nallapati Venkatramaiah
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are: Tanguturi Prakasam—first Chief Minister of Andhra State; Neelam Sanjiva Reddy—first Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh; Chandulal Madhavlal Trivedi—first Governor of Andhra Pradesh; Nallapati Venkatramaiah—first Speaker of Andhra State.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. Rajasekhara Charitram was the first novel in Telugu.
II. Satya Doota was the first Telugu journal.
III. Andhra Prakasika was the first political journal in Andhra.
IV. The Bible was the first book printed in Telugu.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
mcqs.explanation: All four statements are correct. The notes identify Rajasekhara Charitram, Satya Doota, Andhra Prakasika and the Bible as the respective first Telugu novel, journal, political journal and printed book.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The first Andhra Mahasabha or Conference was held at Bapatla on 26 May 1913.
Statement B: Govinda Rao Nanal was the first President of the Hyderabad State Congress.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The first Andhra Mahasabha or Conference was held at Bapatla on 26 May 1913, and Govinda Rao Nanal was the first President of the Hyderabad State Congress.

mcqs.question:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. First widow remarriage in Andhra
B. First Telugu session of the Indian National Congress
C. Andhra Pradesh Legislature became bicameral for the first time
D. First World Telugu Conference
mcqs.explanation: The correct order is A, B, C, D: widow remarriage in 1881, the Telugu session of the INC in 1891, bicameral legislature in 1958, and the World Telugu Conference in 1975.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Satavahanas were the first historical ruling dynasty of the Deccan.
II. Harihara-I was the first ruler of Vijayanagara.
III. Devaraya-I was the first Vijayanagara monarch to enlist Muslims in the army.
IV. The first Muslim invasion of Warangal took place in 1303.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
mcqs.explanation: All four statements are correct according to the historical firsts listed: Satavahanas, Harihara-I, Devaraya-I and the 1303 invasion of Warangal.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(a) First Dutch factory in Andhra
(b) First factory by the English in Andhra
(c) First introduction of Ryotwari
(d) First Indian State to sign the Subsidiary Alliance

List-II
(i) Baramahals
(ii) Hyderabad
(iii) Masulipatnam or Machilipatnam
(iv) Machilipatnam, 1611
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are: Dutch factory—Masulipatnam or Machilipatnam; English factory—Machilipatnam in 1611; Ryotwari—Baramahals; first Indian State to sign the Subsidiary Alliance—Hyderabad.

2.title: Last Rulers and Andhra State CM

mcqs.question: Who was the last Chief Minister of Andhra State?
mcqs.explanation: Bezawada Gopala Reddy was the last Chief Minister of Andhra State.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Bezawada Gopala Reddy served as Chief Minister of Andhra State from 1955 until 1956.
Reason (R): Andhra State merged to form Andhra Pradesh in 1956.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The merger of Andhra State to form Andhra Pradesh in 1956 explains the end of Bezawada Gopala Reddy’s tenure as its Chief Minister.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: Vijayaditya VII was the last king of the Eastern Chalukyas.
Vasanta Raju was the last Reddy king.
Errana was the last king of the Eastern Chalukyas.
Pulomavi III was regarded as the last ruler of the Satavahanas according to the Puranas.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect statement is that Errana was the last king of the Eastern Chalukyas. The correct name is Vijayaditya VII; Errana was the last poet of the Kavitrayam.

mcqs.question: According to the Puranas, who was the last ruler of the Satavahanas?
mcqs.explanation: According to the Puranas, Pulomavi III was the last ruler of the Satavahanas.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Vasanta Raju was the last Reddy king.
Statement B: Errana was the last poet of the Kavitrayam and served as the court poet of Prolaya Vema Reddy.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. Vasanta Raju was the last Reddy king, while Errana was the last poet of the Kavitrayam and the court poet of Prolaya Vema Reddy.

mcqs.question: Which inscription is associated with the last Satavahana king, Pulumavi IV?
mcqs.explanation: The Myakadoni inscription is associated with Pulumavi IV, identified in the notes as the last Satavahana king.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Inscription)
a. Nasik
b. Motupalli
c. Draksharama
d. Tripuranthakam

List-II (Key association)
i. Rudra Deva's success stories
ii. Military achievements of Gautamiputra Satakarni
iii. Ganapatideva
iv. Victorious achievements of Amba Deva

Choose the correct code:
mcqs.explanation: Nasik records Gautamiputra Satakarni's military achievements; Motupalli is associated with Ganapatideva; Draksharama records Rudra Deva's successes; and Tripuranthakam records Amba Deva's victories.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: The Pithapuram inscription mentions Kolleru lake.
The Kalamalla inscription is identified as the first inscription in Sanskrit.
The Pedavegi inscription of Nandi Varma-II records a grant of land to Vishnu.
The Bhattiprolu inscription mentions the Nigama-sabha of the Satavahanas.
mcqs.explanation: The altered detail is the language: the Kalamalla inscription is identified in the notes as the first inscription in Telugu, not Sanskrit.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The Allahabad Pillar inscription mentions Hastivarma.
Reason (R): The Allahabad Pillar inscription was issued by Samudragupta.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are given in the notes: the inscription was issued by Samudragupta and mentions Hastivarma. However, its issuer does not explain why Hastivarma is mentioned.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Brihatpalayanas were feudatories of the Ikshvakus.
Statement B: The Kondamudi Copper Edict is the only inscription about the Brihatpalayanas.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: The notes state both that the Brihatpalayanas were feudatories of the Ikshvakus and that the Kondamudi Copper Edict is the only inscription about them.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Porumamilla inscription gives 12 rules for tank construction.
II. The Santhana Sagaram inscription is related to a tank by Surambika.
III. The Mutnuri inscription records the completion of steps to Pathala Ganga in 1346.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
mcqs.explanation: All three statements are directly supported by the notes: Porumamilla gives 12 tank-construction rules, Santhana Sagaram is linked with Surambika's tank, and Mutnuri records the 1346 completion of the steps to Pathala Ganga.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Inscription)
a. Nagarjunakonda
b. Manchikallu
c. Chejerla
d. Eluru

List-II (Key fact)
i. Mentions 'Munyada', a political employee
ii. Wars between Ikshvakus and Anandagotrikas
iii. Ikshvaku dynasty
aiv. Simhavarma; found near Vijayapuri and similar to Nagarjunakonda

Choose the correct code:
mcqs.explanation: Nagarjunakonda is linked with the Ikshvaku dynasty; Manchikallu is associated with Simhavarma; Chejerla records wars between the Ikshvakus and Anandagotrikas; and Eluru mentions Munyada.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following inscription–fact pairs are correctly matched?

1. Nasik — Ushavadatta invested 2000 Karshapanas in a weaver's guild.
2. Motupalli — Ganapatideva.
3. Allahabad Pillar — Hastivarma.
4. Myakadoni — Pulumavi IV.
mcqs.explanation: All four pairs are correct according to the notes: Nasik records Ushavadatta's investment, Motupalli is linked with Ganapatideva, Allahabad mentions Hastivarma, and Myakadoni is associated with Pulumavi IV.

mcqs.question: In which Ajanta cave can the “Swetagaja Jataka” painting be seen?
mcqs.explanation: The notes state that the “Swetagaja Jataka” painting can be seen in Ajanta Cave No. 10.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: Bhairavakonda was a centre of Saivism.
Bhairavakonda was a centre for the Rajagirika school of Buddhists.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect statement is that Bhairavakonda was a centre for the Rajagirika school of Buddhists. The notes associate Bhairavakonda with Nellore district, eight caves and Saivism; Guntupalli was the centre for the Rajagirika school.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The Nasik Cave Inscription mentions the military achievements of Gautamiputra Satakarni.
Reason (R): It was issued by Gautami Balasri during the period of Vasishtiputra Pulomavi.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true according to the notes. However, the issuer and period do not explain why the inscription mentions Gautamiputra Satakarni’s military achievements.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Ajanta
(b) Nasik
(c) Bhairavakonda
(d) Guntupalli

List-II
(i) Centre for the Rajagirika school of Buddhists
(ii) Nasik Cave Inscription
(iii) “Swetagaja Jataka” painting
(iv) Eight caves and centre of Saivism
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are Ajanta–“Swetagaja Jataka” painting, Nasik–Nasik Cave Inscription, Bhairavakonda–eight caves and centre of Saivism, and Guntupalli–Rajagirika school of Buddhists.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. Guntupalli is near Kamavarapukota.
II. Guntupalli is in Eluru district.
III. Guntupalli was a centre of Saivism.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Statements I and II are correct: Guntupalli is near Kamavarapukota in Eluru district. The notes associate the centre of Saivism with Bhairavakonda, not Guntupalli, so Statement III is incorrect.

mcqs.question: Who authored Rajasekhara Charitram, identified as the first Telugu novel?
mcqs.explanation: Rajasekhara Charitram, identified as the first Telugu novel, was authored by Kandukuri Veeresalingam.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: Gatha Saptasati was authored by Hala.
Madhura Vijayam was authored by Gangadevi.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect statement is the fourth one. Amuktamalyada was authored by Krishnadevaraya, not Tirumalamba.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Jayapa Senani authored Nrittaratnavali.
Reason (R): Jayapa Senani's profession was Gaja Sahini.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true: Nrittaratnavali was authored by Jayapa Senani, whose profession was Gaja Sahini. His profession does not explain his authorship of the work.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Gita Govinda
(b) English-Telugu Dictionary
(c) Eighteen Fifty Seven
(d) Sangita Sudhakaram

List-II
(i) C.P. Brown
(ii) Jayadeva
(iii) S.N. Sen
(iv) Singabhupala II
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are: Gita Govinda–Jayadeva, English-Telugu Dictionary–C.P. Brown, Eighteen Fifty Seven–S.N. Sen, and Sangita Sudhakaram–Singabhupala II.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. Narasimha Puranam was authored by Errana.
II. Ranganatha Ramayana was authored by Gona Buddha Reddy.
III. Narayana Satakam was authored by Potana.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
mcqs.explanation: All three statements are correct. The notes associate Narasimha Puranam with Errana, Ranganatha Ramayana with Gona Buddha Reddy, and Narayana Satakam with Potana.

mcqs.question: Which temple is regarded as the oldest Saivite temple?
mcqs.explanation: Parasurameswara Temple at Gudimallam is identified as the oldest Saivite temple.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: The Navabrahma temple complex at Alampur consists of nine temples.
The Thousand Pillars Temple at Anamakonda was built by Rudradeva.
The Ramappa Temple at Palampet was constructed by Krishnadevaraya.
The Ramappa Temple at Palampet was built by Recharla Rudra in 1213 AD.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect detail is the builder of the Ramappa Temple. It was built by Recharla Rudra in 1213 AD; Krishnadevaraya constructed the Hazara Ramaswamy Temple at Hampi.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Lepakshi is famous for Vijayanagara school paintings.
Reason (R): Lepakshi is also known for its huge stone bull.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true, but the presence of a huge stone bull does not explain why Lepakshi is famous for Vijayanagara school paintings.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Parasurameswara Temple
(b) Navabrahma Temple complex
(c) Ramappa Temple
(d) Surya Temple

List-II
(i) Arasavalli
(ii) Gudimallam
(iii) Palampet
(iv) Alampur
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are Parasurameswara–Gudimallam, Navabrahma–Alampur, Ramappa–Palampet and Surya–Arasavalli.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:

I. The Virupaksha Temple is a famous temple at Hampi.
II. The Bhimeshwara Temple stands on the banks of the Godavari and was built by Ammaraju of the Eastern Chalukyas.
III. The Pushpa Bhadra Swami Temple at Nagarjuna Konda was constructed by Virapurushadatta of the Ikshvaku period.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
mcqs.explanation: All three statements are correct: Virupaksha is at Hampi, Bhimeshwara was built by Ammaraju on the Godavari banks, and Pushpa Bhadra Swami was constructed by Virapurushadatta at Nagarjuna Konda.

mcqs.question: The main seat of the goddess Vasavi was located at:
mcqs.explanation: According to the notes, Penugonda was the main seat of the goddess Vasavi, associated with the Arya Vysya community.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: Virupaksha was the family god of the Vijayanagara people and had a famous temple at Hampi.
Pushpa Bhadra Swami temple at Nagarjunakonda was constructed by Elisiri.
The Sarvadevadhikasam temple at Nagarjunakonda was built by Elisiri.
Chitraratha Swamy was the family deity of the Salankayanas.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect statement attributes the Pushpa Bhadra Swami temple to Elisiri. The notes state that it was constructed by Virapurushadatta, while Elisiri built the Sarvadevadhikasam temple.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Bappa Bhattaraka was associated with the Salankayanas.
Reason (R): The term Bappa Bhattaraka means “consideration of father as God.”
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are given in the notes: Bappa Bhattaraka is associated with the Salankayanas, and the term means “consideration of father as God.” The meaning does not explain the historical association itself.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Hariti
(b) Vasavi
(c) Virupaksha
(d) Chitraratha Swamy

List-II
(i) Vijayanagara people
(ii) Arya Vysya community
(iii) Early Chalukyas
(iv) Salankayanas
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are Hariti–Early Chalukyas, Vasavi–Arya Vysya community, Virupaksha–Vijayanagara people, and Chitraratha Swamy–Salankayanas.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:

I. Sriparvata Swamy of the Vishnukundins was identified with Buddha by N. Venkata Ramanaiah.
II. Kumara Swami was the Ikshvaku commander Elisiri at Nagarjunakonda.
III. The Ashtabhuja Narayana temple was located at Nagarjunakonda.
IV. A land grant to Vishnu was mentioned in the Pedavegi inscription of Nandi Varma-II.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
mcqs.explanation: All four statements are supported by the notes: they associate Sriparvata Swamy with the Vishnukundins, identify Elisiri as the Ikshvaku commander, locate the Ashtabhuja Narayana temple at Nagarjunakonda, and mention the Vishnu land grant in the Pedavegi inscription of Nandi Varma-II.

mcqs.question: Motupalli was also known as which of the following?
mcqs.explanation: The notes state that Motupalli, under the Kakatiyas, was also called Desiyakondapattanam.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about Machilipatnam or Masulipatnam is incorrect?
options: It was the most famous port for textile trade.
It was associated with Golconda during the 16th–17th centuries.
It was famous for diamond trade in the 1600s.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect detail is the name Kantakossyla. The notes state that Ptolemy called Machilipatnam or Masulipatnam Mysolia, while Kantakossyla was the name associated with Ghantasala.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Ghantasala was an important port during the Ikshvaku period.
Reason (R): Claudius Ptolemy mentioned Ghantasala as the maritime emporium Kantakossyla.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are given in the notes. Ghantasala was an important Ikshvaku port, and Ptolemy mentioned it as the maritime emporium Kantakossyla.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(a) Motupalli
(b) Motupalli
(c) Machilipatnam / Masulipatnam
(d) Visakhapatnam

List-II
(i) Western seaport under the Satavahanas
(ii) Most famous for textile trade and famous for diamond trade
(iii) Port associated with the Kakatiyas
(iv) Port facilitating transportation and trade of agricultural products in the 19th century
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are: Motupalli–Kakatiyas, Motupalli–Satavahanas as a western seaport, Machilipatnam/Masulipatnam–textile and diamond trade, and Visakhapatnam–19th-century agricultural-product transport and trade.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Motupalli was an important port under the Reddys, and Mallaya Reddy occupied it.
Statement B: Somaya issued an ‘Abhaya Sasana’ for the development of trade at Motupalli.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true according to the notes. Motupalli was occupied by Mallaya Reddy, and Somaya issued an ‘Abhaya Sasana’ for trade development.

mcqs.question: In which year was the English East India Company factory established at Machilipatnam?
mcqs.explanation: The English East India Company established its factory at Machilipatnam in 1611, with permission from Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: Tavernier was a 17th-century trader who visited Andhra mines in search of precious stones and diamonds.
Marco Polo visited Motupalli port during the Kakatiya period of Rudramadevi.
Haravilasam was dedicated to Tippayya Setti by Marco Polo.
Tippayya Setti, also known as Avachi Tippayya, was famous for overseas trade during the Reddy period.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect detail is the author of the dedication. Srinatha dedicated Haravilasam to Tippayya Setti; it was not dedicated by Marco Polo.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Guilds or Srenulu helped the development of trade during the Satavahana period.
Reason (R): Nigamalu were trade guilds during the Ikshvaku period.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true according to the notes. However, the role of Nigamalu during the Ikshvaku period does not explain the role of Srenulu during the Satavahana period.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(a) Tavernier
(b) Tippayya Setti / Avachi Tippayya
(c) Marco Polo
(d) Moturpha

List-II
(i) Tax on trade and occupations
(ii) 17th-century trader who visited Andhra mines
(iii) Famous for overseas trade during the Reddy period
(iv) Visited Motupalli port
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are: Tavernier–17th-century trader who visited Andhra mines; Tippayya Setti–overseas trade during the Reddy period; Marco Polo–Motupalli port; Moturpha–tax on trade and occupations.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. Moturpha was a tax on trade and occupations.
II. Roman coins were found at Bhattiprolu and Nagarjuna Konda.
III. Arikamedu was a Roman trade centre on the western side.
IV. Coins of Pulomavi and Yagnasri indicate Satavahana maritime trade.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Statements I, II and IV are correct. Statement III is incorrect because the notes identify Arikamedu as a Roman trade centre on the eastern side.

10.title: Administrative Officers and Bodies Across Eras

mcqs.question: In the Satavahana administration, who administered the Aharas?
mcqs.explanation: The notes state that Satavahana Amatyas administered the Aharas.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements regarding Kakatiya administration is incorrect?
options: Ayagarlu were twelve officials who enjoyed land without any cess or tax.
Bahathara Viyog was the collective name of all administration departments.
Bahathara Viyogaduipathi held supreme authority over all departments.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect detail is the number of Kakatiya Village Officers. The notes state that their number was twelve, not ten.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The Collector’s administration came into existence in 1794 in place of the Board of Revenue.
Reason (R): The Office of Collector was introduced in the North Sarkar region in 1802.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are given in the notes as separate facts. The 1802 introduction of the Office of Collector does not explain the 1794 replacement of the Board of Revenue.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Pradvivaka
(b) Srinatha
(c) G.N. Taylor
(d) V. Veeranna

List-II
(i) Andhra officer who helped Sir Arthur Cotton in Godavari Barrage construction
(ii) Sub-Collector of Rajahmundry who opened Anglo-vernacular schools
(iii) Advisor to the king in judiciary
(iv) Educational officer in the court of Pedakomati Vema Reddy
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are Pradvivaka–advisor to the king in judiciary, Srinatha–educational officer, G.N. Taylor–Sub-Collector of Rajahmundry, and V. Veeranna–helper in Godavari Barrage construction.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements about Satavahana administration:

I. The Mantri Parishad helped the king in administration.
II. The Nigama Sabha or Nigama Subhas looked after the administration of cities and towns.
III. The Gramani had jurisdiction over five or ten villages.
IV. The Gaaha Pati was a representative of farmers.
mcqs.explanation: All four statements are directly supported by the notes: the Mantri Parishad assisted the king, the Nigama Sabha administered cities and towns, the Gramani covered five or ten villages, and the Gaaha Pati represented farmers.

11.title: Telugu Language, Scripts and Literary Milestones

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Satavahana common people's language
(b) Salankayana language from Sanskrit onwards
(c) Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi official language
(d) Language of Sangam literature

List-II
(i) Tamil
(ii) Desi Bhaasha
(iii) Telugu
(iv) Sanskrit
mcqs.explanation: Satavahana common people's language was Desi Bhaasha, Salankayana used Sanskrit onwards, Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi had Telugu as their official language, and Sangam literature was in Tamil.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: Prakrit was the official language of the Satavahanas.
Three of the eight Salankayana inscriptions were in Prakrit.
Telugu became the official language of Andhra Pradesh from 1956.
Early Ikshvaku inscriptions were in Prakrit.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect detail is the year 1956. Telugu became the official language of Andhra Pradesh from 1966.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): All Satavahana inscriptions were written in Prakrit using the Brahmi script.
Reason (R): Prakrit was the official language of the Satavahanas.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true: Satavahana inscriptions were in Prakrit and Brahmi script, and Prakrit was the Satavahana official language. However, the official-language status of Prakrit does not explain the use of the Brahmi script.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. Kalamalla inscription was the first Telugu inscription.
II. Rajasekhara Charitram was the first Telugu novel.
III. Satya Doota was the first Telugu journal and was associated with Bellary.
IV. C. P. Brown was associated with the first English-Telugu dictionary.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
mcqs.explanation: All four statements are correct. The notes identify Kalamalla as the first Telugu inscription, Rajasekhara Charitram as the first Telugu novel, Satya Doota of Bellary as the first Telugu journal, and C. P. Brown with the first English-Telugu dictionary.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The first World Telugu Conference was held in 1975.
Statement B: Sri Krishnadevaraya Bhasha Nilayam in Hyderabad was established in 1901 as the first Telugu library.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The first World Telugu Conference was held in 1975, while Sri Krishnadevaraya Bhasha Nilayam in Hyderabad dates to 1901 and is identified as the first Telugu library.

mcqs.question: Who was the queen of Bobbili associated with the Battle of Bobbili (1757)?
mcqs.explanation: Mallamma Devi was the queen of Bobbili associated with the Battle of Bobbili in 1757.

The Battle of Raichur was fought in 1520 and was the greatest battle fought by Sri Krishnadevaraya.

Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true

mcqs.question: Moturpha was which of the following?
options: A Kakatiya cess on dry lands
A British tax on trade and occupations in 1861

mcqs.question: Karpanamulu were which type of coins associated with the Satavahanas?
mcqs.explanation: Karpanamulu are identified in the notes as Satavahana copper coins.

Roman coins were found at Bhattiprolu and Amaravati.

mcqs.explanation: The notes state that Santamula-I of the Ikshvaku dynasty issued crores of gold coins.

mcqs.question: Which of the following was the first Telugu journal?
mcqs.explanation: Satya Doota was the first Telugu journal. It was associated with the Christian Association of Bellary and was published from Bellary.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: Vivekavardhini was a journal started by Kandukuri Veeresalingam in 1874.
Satihita Bodhini was a monthly magazine started by Kandukuri Veeresalingam in 1886.
Brahma Prakasika was a journal edited by Ragupati Venkataratnam Naidu in 1886.
Satyasamvardhini was a journal started by Kandukuri Veeresalingam in 1891.

mcqs.question:

options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A

mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true: Desha Matha strongly supported the Home Rule Movement and was edited by Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham. The editorship does not, by itself, explain the stated political support.

mcqs.explanation: All three statements are correct. Vahini is linked with N.G. Ranga and peasant leaders, Rayyat was edited by M. Narasinga Rao, and Asamarthuni Yatra was T. Gopichand’s 1947 novel celebrated as the first psychological novel in Telugu literature.

mcqs.explanation: The notes associate Krishna Patrika with Mutnuri Krishna Rao.
